findings.limitation: Counts come from the release's sample list: one sample is one barcode, and one patient can have several samples. Presence in a file means the sample appears there; it says nothing about data quality or completeness inside the file. Survival presence says nothing about follow-up length; events are overall-survival deaths.
next_actions: State which sample types the count covers (primary tumor, normal tissue, metastasis) so readers can reproduce it.
Check data quality inside the file, not just presence, before relying on it.

examples.label: In the denominator but not counted

findings.limitation: Presence in a file means the sample appears there; it says nothing about data quality or completeness inside the file. A clinical field counts as recorded when it holds a value (not blank or 'not available'); the values themselves were not verified. Where several columns hold the same field, the one with the most recorded values is used unless overridden, which favors completeness over how definitive the measurement is.
next_actions: Check data quality inside the field, not just counts, before relying on the ranking.
Restrict the question to the 421 samples that match, or choose a layer or field with better coverage.
Restate the claim with the measured figure (421 of 844).

robustness.alt_rule: count samples with no recorded value in the denominator too

suggested_correction.text: Luminal A is the largest RNA subtype, accounting for about 49.9% of primary tumors with an RNA subtype call.
suggested_correction.basis: The sentence says 62%; the data shows 49.9% (421 of 844). Only that number was replaced, so the rest of the wording is the author's.
